attempts.summary: Configured node3 with a single gateway address (10.50.10.1) that reaches node4's private network with automatic router failover. node1 and node2 each run VyOS with interfaces on both node3's segment (10.50.10.0/24, eth1) and node4's segment (10.50.20.0/24, eth2). A keepalived VRRP group per segment provides virtual gateway IPs (10.50.10.1 on node3's segment, 10.50.20.1 on node4's segment); node1 is priority 200 (preferred/preemptive master), node2 is priority 100 (backup). node3 has one static route to 10.50.20.0/24 via 10.50.10.1 — a single, always-available gateway address regardless of which physical router is up. node4 has the symmetric static route back via 10.50.20.1 so replies traverse correctly. Verified live failover: rebooted node1 (the preferred router) while running continuous pings from node3 to node4 — node2 took over as MASTER on both VRRP groups within ~1s, all 64 pings succeeded (0% loss), and when node1 came back it reclaimed MASTER via VRRP preemption as designed. All four nodes (node1-node4) were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; each showed a changed boot_id and, after recovery, correct VRRP state (node1 MASTER, node2 BACKUP), persisted IP/route configuration, and successful node3↔node4 ICMP connectivity.
